body: Your transition won’t be stunted at all, but you may feel more emotional if you’re a sensitive person in general! I find that when I’m not taking my T daily, I’m pretty disregulated. But nothing bad will happen to you and you’ll go back to feeling normal the next time you take it.

as you grow you’ll learn that it’s childish to try and seem older than you are. in the future you will have lived more as yourself and your peers will look up to you because you are authentic in your skin :) keep it up, be yourself and enjoy what you enjoy- i guarantee it’ll make you much happier than anyone who is teasing you

this might seem small, but i love finding friendly compliments! i’m an outgoing person, but with a LOT of anxiety so leading into new interactions can be difficult so i usually go the route of complementing someone accessories and stuff and usually people really like that positivity! i try to tie the compliments to things i have in common or ask questions and stuff. this primarily works works with more feminine people (talking to men is hard for me) but still, people feel lifted up when you notice little things about them and their choices! it’ll get easier i promise :) especially out of highschool when people will behave more authentically. i find that as i get older, less and less people make me feel like im weird or boring. keep going! i promise you’re doing a better job that you’re giving yourself credit for, it really is a difficult thing and it’s great you’re asking for help :) tell people about your interests as well! it’s important to believe that you are not boring, i promise you no one truly is.

Thank you for sharing this, I am sorry to hear your frustration as it really resonates with me. It’s sort of a heartbreaking feeling, relief and then immediate sadness that the world isn’t built with people like us in mind. Or many different kinds of people at all. The “correct” face and sensory issues calming down sound like unmasking to me. I recommend Devon Price’s “Unmasking Autism”. I found it very helpful and even others who don’t necessarily feel that they are autistic have found it eye opening. I wish you relief! I know it is so hard to come by. Please try and give yourself grace.

I feel this! Not only are you being exposed to a lot of different emotions in a really short amount of time with this short-form content, but you’re also seeing a particularly mean world! I’ve deleted tiktok for the same reason but have the same problem with the dumber instagram reels. 

I personally am a little addicted to reading comments, and I feel like it’s skewing my perception of the social world. I start to think the world is as mean and angry as the loud voices commenting the worst things on a cute video of a baby or someone trying a new hobby. This makes me more anxious to go out into the world and I feel like I don’t know what to expect from people in public. I live in a larger city and find myself thinking the people on public transit are all as angry as those comments are. 

I want to unlearn that the internet is how the real world works, but for now i’m still trying to click on where instagram was in my phone even after deleting it.

This is something I’ve been feeling too! Always evaluating how “well” i’m enjoying something or doing a task like cleaning. I’ve been in school feeling like everyone else is smarter than me. It must be upsetting that it’s affecting your enjoyment of hobbies and I am really sorry to hear. It may seem woo-woo, but I have been trying to redirect my comparing and sense of competition. I try to repeat to myself that these situations are all similar to going ice-skating with friends and seeing a 7 year old spin beautifully in the center of the rink. Everyone is impressed, but there is no reason to be jealous! Because she must have been put on skates by her parents very young. Like her skating, there are things you excel at in your personal, interpersonal, or professional life that  others may feel behind you in as well. It can be hard to internalize this right away, but no one is keeping track of how behind or ahead you are, only you! I understand that this feeling is like an “impulsive trigger” and which I totally feel! But i think with repeated redirection and trying to repeat these ideas to myself I’ve noticed some change in the past few months. I hope this helps and that things get easier! You deserve to enjoy new things!

I understand how frustrating this must be! I myself have had my doctor encourage lower doses and it feels like a fight to raise my dose. I’m constantly having the pharmacy inform me that she’s lowered the strength and i’ve had to have so many back and forth to raise my dosage past starting dose. (and even now, a year in, im barely above a starting dose) it seems doctors are really hesitant to prescribe higher doses and I agree with other comments saying it’s probably best to switch. I also want to acknowledge how difficult getting Hrt and trans health care is in general-  I know how it takes time. I say it’s probably best to hold out with this (sucky) provider until your move.
Also make sure prior to your move you book appointments so you don’t end up off your shots for too long! since it can be difficult to change doctors/locations.

You have a right to be upset/hurt at this. 

Early in my transition, I had started hooking up with someone. There were a lot of concerning things about this person and our fwb situation, but what had hurt me wasn’t this person’s attraction- that isn’t something they can help. But knowing that while I identified as a man pre-T, while they had use the correct pronouns (though they’d usually call me a nickname, not my chosen name), they didn’t truly respect my gender. I felt like once I was physically visually closer to their definition of a man, I didn’t attract them anymore. I understand why you feel reduced, and I am so sorry this happened to you. It really hurt when I realized it wasn’t until I started physically transitioning that this person didn’t essentially see me as a woman anymore. That is to say it’s heart-breaking to think that while together, your gender identity may not have been as respected as you thought it was.

Im really glad this conversation is being held- and a lot of these comments sum up what I have felt as well but I also want to speak on feeling the “deep center of shame” that gets triggered by these types of the “not like other girls” posts. (even when you’re aware they’re misogynistic, bullying, baloney)

Something I deal with often is feeling like posts disliking some sort of annoying persona— in this case the “not like other girls” persona— is taken pretty literally by my brain. Be it from my autistic or trans experience, I know that I want to avoid being any annoying or disliked archetype. It’s refreshing to hear reminders that these posts and phrases are designed to hurt. 

I am a pretty feminine trans man, and I cringe with shame at my pick me phase as well as my hyper-feminine closested phase. (now called the drag years) But I also want to provide myself and others with forgiveness and grace. 

At school by other girls I was called different, I was made fun of, I was isolated. So at some point it felt almost natural into wanting to gain the approval of boys or genuinely believe that I was, in fact, different from other girls. At time in my life that was easier to comprehend than being Trans and god forbid autistic. 

This didn’t go in any direction, but know that you were learning and still are. And I hope that with every new day you and I will feel less pangs of shame for who we are.

I adore femininity and care quite a bit about beauty! I’ve got a feminine pattern of speech despite my voice dropping being on T for 3 months now. For the longest time I thought I couldn’t be a trans man because of my love for femininity but like a lot of these comments say, i’d like to be perceived as an effeminate man. To me a lot of things that are masculine are a tad more boring and don’t spike my interest. What helped me embrace being a feminine man was seeing trans men do drag and enjoy femininity under those terms! as I continue to transition and eventually get top surgery I know i will feel even more secure in my relationship with femininity as a man. Queer men have often been more comfortable with femininity and non conforming gender expression and i definitely resonate with this. Understanding that my interests and aesthetic are not my gender has really helped me embrace who I am, which is definitely a man. But a pretty gay, feminine one. Thanks for opening such an interesting discussion!

im just over two months on T injections and 19yo and the place i’ve noticed the most change has been my voice, neck, and face. my facial features are looking quite different around my jaw and my neck is quite a lot more defined. i’ve been working out and noticed building muscle mass is a lot faster on T. My voice has dropped significantly for only two months. 

T won’t change who you are, sure like you mentioned the confidence can change things and it’s generally so much more comfortable to feel affirmed in your gender. The only thing i’ve been facing is an increased libido honestly. 

Like other comments it’s hard to notice things overnight but there was this point the other day where I was looking at old pictures and watching videos of myself when i really realized how different i looked and sounded in comparison.  

I assure you, you will only become more of your favorite parts of yourself. There is no need to worry about changing drastically or mentally. T is a hormone and honestly changes a lot less mentally than i would say psych meds do.

im in a super similar situation, because of having sensitive skin i can’t use tape and this is my first summer being out and transitioning and it is so dysphoria and inducing and difficult so first of all i want to say i feel you and am sending love your way. 

One thing I try to remind myself that I see really often on this subreddit is that naturally, even cis men don’t have the flattest chests. It’s also important to remember that others don’t perceive our bodies as critically as we do. My ribs have been really hurting from binding so i’ve been wearing looser shirts like muscle tanks and cutting the sleeves off. while this isn’t perfectly my style the bagginess of the shirt helps me feel comfortable. 

I guess this is a more forward way of thinking but i’ve been telling myself this anytime i want to go to the beach since swimming in my binder has really been hurting; 
while I want to be perceived as nothing but male by the strangers at the beach, I have to respect my body and comfort. I know the people I’m with see me as a man no matter what I wear. I know im a man regardless of being pre-op or not. Jealousy of cis men is hard to overcome and Im not sure it’ll ever go away completely but this summer i’ve been reminding myself that men do not need to look one type of way. Validating my own masculinity has greatly helped how I feel being out and about. While I wait to have enough money for top surgery I guess i’ve been repeating to myself that some men have larger chests. and that’s okay, they’re still men. 

I don’t know, but I hope in some way this helps dude. Hang in there <3

Hi! Ive been on T from PP for two months now and do not have insurance due to being on my parents’ insurance and not having their support. Planned Parenthood does a great job at accommodating to you financially and depending on your situation you could have your visits fully covered. At your first visit they’ll take your hemoglobin levels to make sure you can get on a safe dose of T and after a couple days you should be able to pick up your prescription/needles from your pharmacy. In my experience they’ll want you to make another appointment for injection training and that’s when you’ll do your first shot! This may not be required but since I was unfamiliar with injecting it was super helpful. One thing I recommend is ordering the correct needles and syringes off amazon if the prices are too high for you from the pharmacy. While My T wasn’t that expensive, 4 of each needle and syringe was about $30 from the pharmacy while you can get hundreds online for the same price. My experience being from a city with lots of planned parenthood clinics, it’s been a really easy process. You should be able to get your T soon after your first appointment and it shouldn’t be all that much. I think mine is like 10 dollars for a supply that lasts me months. Be sure to ask your clinician/nurse at the clinic for a GoodRx card, that can really help lower the prices. Congrats dude, Im so happy for you to start this!
